summary: This task's own workspace (worker/task-20260727-064948-...) has zero commits and an empty diff against master; per PROGRESS.md the worker correctly identified that the real fix belongs on PR #110's branch (worker/task-20260727-061625-build-server-resource-governor--queued-d) and, since git disallows checking out that branch a second time, applied and committed the fix there instead (commit 884f634), which I located and reviewed directly. The commit is a genuine, correctly scoped fix for the TOCTOU race in resource_governor.py's dispatch_one(): row selection via next_queued_task() previously ran before dc.acquire_dispatch_lock() was acquired, so two concurrent callers could both select and spawn the same queued row; the fix moves row selection, the free-slot check, the real spawn, and the umr_tasks status update (which takes the row out of 'queued') all inside the single acquire_dispatch_lock() critical section, matching dispatch_core.py's own documented locking contract. I confirmed acquire_dispatch_lock() is a real cross-process fcntl.flock (not just an in-process lock), so the fix genuinely closes the race for separate systemd/cron-invoked processes, not just threads. I ran the full test_resource_governor.py suite (16 passed) and independently reverse-verified the new concurrency test by reverting resource_governor.py to the pre-fix version and re-running it: it fails deterministically (2 dispatches instead of 1) against the old code and passes against the fix, confirming the test is real and not a placebo. PR #110's file list (resource_governor.py, superboss-register.py, veridian-task-watchdog.py, a systemd unit file, docs, and tests) touches no migrations/schema/SQL, no .github/workflows, no auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths, and no .env files, and this specific commit is a small net-positive diff (19 insertions/11 deletions in the source file plus a pure test addition) -- consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. Note for record-keeping: during review I incidentally found and cleaned up a leftover unrelated stash-pop conflict in that workspace (an old PROGRESS.md merge stash from an unrelated 2026-07-23 task) that a stray `git stash`/`git stash pop` of mine surfaced; I reset it back to a clean working tree without dropping the pre-existing stash entry, so no data was lost, but this is unrelated to the fix itself.
